title: Martian dynamo test programme
scope: Thirty proposals from a user-supplied research synthesis, reorganized into compatible dimensions. Original project test designs with a targeted primary-source assessment; not a complete literature audit or a ranking of theories.
execution_status: All thirty proposed discriminating tests are planned, not executed. Existing regional and thermal calculations are explicitly separate building blocks.
provenance: The supplied synthesis is a discovery aid, not a source of established results. No private internship material, external code, new dataset or publisher full text is incorporated.

groups.title: When was it active?
groups.description: Separate dated activity, permanent shutdown and gaps in the preserved record.

groups.title: What could power it?
groups.description: Energy sources, boundary conditions and shutdown behavior play different roles.

groups.title: What shape was the field?
groups.description: Compare the generated field with what rocks would record over time.

groups.title: What did the rocks preserve?
groups.description: Acquisition, alteration, shock, burial and measurement can change the observed contrast.

groups.title: What does today’s interior constrain?
groups.description: Present structure is an endpoint for evolution models, not a direct ancient measurement.

tests.title: Early permanent shutdown
tests.claim: The dynamo stopped permanently around 4.1–4.0 Ga.
tests.test: Search for younger, independently dated remanence attributable to a global field; compare active-field and no-dynamo predictions under the same recording and detection model.
tests.required_inputs: Magnetization ages, local crustal-field estimates, carrier histories and calibrated detection limits.
tests.discriminator: A secure younger global-field record would contradict permanent shutdown at the proposed age.
tests.limits: A weak or null local field cannot establish shutdown: erasure, burial, cancellation and insufficient resolution remain alternatives.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Activity at early and late epochs
tests.claim: Magnetic observations have been interpreted as activity at about 4.5 and 3.7 Ga.
tests.test: Audit the relation between mapped unit age, magnetic source depth and remanence acquisition age at both epochs.
tests.required_inputs: Unit chronology, subsurface geometry, component origin and age uncertainties.
tests.discriminator: Failure of an age-to-magnetization association removes that particular timing constraint.
tests.limits: Two active epochs do not demonstrate continuous activity in between; surface age need not date buried magnetization.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Long-lived activity with reversals
tests.claim: A reversing dynamo could leave weak basin fields through cancellation during cooling.
tests.test: Predict the same basins at several altitudes for reversing, stable, intermittent and extinguished histories; include noise and mineral-source uncertainty.
tests.required_inputs: Cooling and acquisition kernels, source mineralogy, excavation geometry, field histories and measurement response.
tests.discriminator: A shared observation model must reproduce both strong surrounding fields and weak basin interiors, including resolvable spatial structure.
tests.limits: The reversal rate is a model parameter, not a measured Martian time series. Mantle excavation alone is not tested under an absent dynamo in the 2025 abstract.
tests.building_block: The existing thermal column supplies synthetic temperature histories only; no remanence or orbital-field calculation is connected yet.

tests.title: Distinct ALH 84001 recording episodes
tests.claim: Separate magnetic components may record different field directions during the rock’s history.
tests.test: Build a component-level ledger of carrier, petrographic context, direction, laboratory treatment and event-age association before comparing episodes.
tests.required_inputs: Published component measurements, age links, uncertainty and alteration/handling history; reuse permission for any data import.
tests.discriminator: Age-resolved, independent components can test directional changes; inconsistent component assignments weaken the inference.
tests.limits: Dates may be assigned by association, not measured for each magnetic grain. Components from one rock are not independent global events.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Hesperian dynamo activity
tests.claim: Some young magnetic sources could require activity after the main early interval.
tests.test: Separate intrusive emplacement ages from remanence ages and test whether local crustal fields could explain acquisition.
tests.required_inputs: Source geometry, intrusion chronology, carrier stability and local-field bounds.
tests.discriminator: A securely dated young global-field signal challenges early permanent shutdown.
tests.limits: Later activity can coexist with an earlier dynamo. Young surface units alone do not date the magnetic source.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Weak activity during basin formation
tests.claim: The dynamo may have been active but weak while major basins formed.
tests.test: Fit field-intensity histories jointly with recording efficiency, instead of treating orbital contrast as a direct intensity ratio.
tests.required_inputs: Calibrated recording efficiencies, comparable source volumes, thermal histories and age constraints.
tests.discriminator: A weak-field history must explain independent intensity constraints as well as basin morphology.
tests.limits: Orbital anomaly amplitude also depends on geometry, mineral abundance and cancellation. The report’s numerical intensity claims remain unaudited.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Impact-controlled onset or interruption
tests.claim: Major impacts could change the timing of core dynamo activity.
tests.test: Link an impact chronology to mantle/core energy evolution, then compare predicted interruptions with independently dated remanence.
tests.required_inputs: Impact energy deposition, core entropy budget, transport times and magnetic ages.
tests.discriminator: A proposed event must produce a physically sufficient core response at the required time.
tests.limits: Local impact demagnetization does not demonstrate core dynamo shutdown or restart.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Intermittent dynamo episodes
tests.claim: Thermal or compositional evolution could permit more than one active interval.
tests.test: Calculate the energy budget and restart conditions, then compare a dated episode model against continuous and permanently extinct alternatives.
tests.required_inputs: Core/mantle histories, dynamo thresholds, hysteresis assumptions and dated recording windows.
tests.discriminator: An interval model must be energetically possible and predict observations beyond those used to choose the intervals.
tests.limits: A gap in preserved magnetic records is not evidence that the dynamo was off.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Thermal convection under a stagnant lid
tests.claim: Core cooling may power convection without sustained plate tectonics.
tests.test: Evaluate entropy available for dynamo action across defensible core conductivity and mantle heat-flow histories.
tests.required_inputs: Core composition, thermal conductivity, initial temperatures, mantle rheology and energy/entropy equations.
tests.discriminator: A specified parameter set fails if it cannot power the independently required active intervals.
tests.limits: Lifetime depends on assumptions. A universal 3.7 Ga cutoff does not follow from the conductivity paper reviewed here.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Early mobile lid followed by stagnation
tests.claim: Early mobile-lid heat loss might support a dynamo before a transition to a stagnant lid.
tests.test: Compare the thermal consequences with independent tectonic and chronological observations under the same interior parameters.
tests.required_inputs: Lid-transition timing, heat transport, crustal reconstruction and dynamo constraints.
tests.discriminator: The proposed transition must fit both the energy budget and independent geological evidence.
tests.limits: Magnetic stripes alone do not establish plate tectonics; lithological contrasts and acquisition histories can produce structure.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Impact suppression of convection
tests.claim: Impact heating or stratification could suppress the core dynamo.
tests.test: Propagate impact heating through a core/mantle evolution calculation and compare suppression duration with dated records.
tests.required_inputs: Deposited energy, mixing, stable stratification and core cooling after the event.
tests.discriminator: A claimed shutdown requires enough suppression for the relevant interval within allowable impact parameters.
tests.limits: Crustal shock resetting and global loss of dynamo power are separate processes.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Impact-triggered dynamo activity
tests.claim: An impact could create conditions for a transient dynamo episode.
tests.test: Predict the onset, duration and power of the episode, including the transport delay between impact and core response.
tests.required_inputs: Impact history, mantle/core coupling and an independently constrained magnetic recording window.
tests.discriminator: An episode shorter than a securely required continuous recording interval would fail that timing test.
tests.limits: A short episode does not refute all late activity; the relevant event ages must first be matched.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Dynamo in a silicate magma ocean
tests.claim: An early conducting silicate layer might generate a magnetic field.
tests.test: Test electrical conductivity, convection and field amplitude for a specified layer lifetime against early recording constraints.
tests.required_inputs: Silicate conductivity, melt depth, convective speeds, cooling history and early magnetization ages.
tests.discriminator: The layer must sustain induction and a surface field during the recording interval.
tests.limits: A present-day solid inner core does not by itself exclude an ancient dynamo outside the metallic core.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Basal molten layer as a thermal blanket
tests.role: Boundary condition, not a dynamo engine
tests.claim: A molten silicate layer may alter heat extraction from the core.
tests.test: Include the layer in a coupled thermal/entropy model and compare with a no-layer case using identical other assumptions.
tests.required_inputs: Layer thickness, material properties, seismic constraints and heat transport.
tests.discriminator: A particular layer history fails if it prevents independently required dynamo activity or violates interior constraints.
tests.limits: Its present existence would not establish its ancient thickness or thermal effect. Do not add this as an independent dynamo mechanism.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Inner-core compositional buoyancy
tests.claim: Solidification could release buoyancy and contribute to dynamo power.
tests.test: Jointly model inner-core growth, light-element partitioning and the entropy budget before comparing the active intervals.
tests.required_inputs: Core composition, phase diagram, growth age and present-day seismic bounds.
tests.discriminator: Growth must begin early enough and supply enough buoyancy for the proposed recording interval.
tests.limits: A proposed present-day inner core does not date its nucleation. The 2025 correction changes a reference, not the detection claim.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Iron snow and remelting
tests.claim: Iron crystallization near the top of the core could affect compositional convection.
tests.test: Trace snow formation, settling and remelting with a composition-dependent phase diagram and entropy balance.
tests.required_inputs: Core composition, liquidus, transport and thermal evolution.
tests.discriminator: The selected regime must sustain the required field without imposing incompatible stratification.
tests.limits: A threshold from a binary alloy cannot be applied universally to Mars’s multicomponent core.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Conductivity and stable stratification
tests.role: Material constraint, not a separate engine
tests.claim: Thermal conductivity influences conductive losses and the onset of convection.
tests.test: Propagate measurement and extrapolation uncertainties into coupled thermal histories; state elapsed time and absolute ages separately.
tests.required_inputs: Solid-to-liquid extrapolation, composition, pressure/temperature dependence and mantle parameters.
tests.discriminator: An energy source must clear the entropy requirement over the inferred active interval for the chosen parameters.
tests.limits: Hsieh et al. extrapolate laboratory results to liquid-core conditions. Mantle assumptions also change the modeled lifetime.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Light-oxide exsolution
tests.claim: Exsolution of light components could provide buoyancy if permitted by Martian core chemistry.
tests.test: First establish a Mars-relevant solubility and partitioning model, then calculate the available energy through time.
tests.required_inputs: Experimental phase relations, core composition, cooling path and energy conversion.
tests.discriminator: If admissible compositions do not exsolve the necessary mass at the required time, that specified mechanism fails.
tests.limits: This is an unverified lead in the supplied report. No dedicated Mars-specific supporting primary source has been established in this assessment.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Subcritical behavior and hysteresis
tests.role: Dynamo response, not an energy source
tests.claim: A field might persist below its onset threshold or restart at a different threshold.
tests.test: Perform calibrated magnetohydrodynamic parameter sweeps with controlled initial states and available power.
tests.required_inputs: Dynamo equations, diffusivities, boundary conditions, convergence checks and physical scaling.
tests.discriminator: A proposed hysteresis history must be reproducible and compatible with the interior energy budget.
tests.limits: Hysteresis cannot supply missing energy; a conductive crustal column does not simulate this mechanism.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Hemispheric dynamo in a spherical shell
tests.claim: Uneven heat extraction at the core–mantle boundary could concentrate field in one hemisphere.
tests.test: Compare time-integrated magnetization with the spatial observations over realistic acquisition windows.
tests.required_inputs: Boundary heat-flow pattern, dynamo solution, reversal history and acquisition durations.
tests.discriminator: The model must retain sufficient hemispheric contrast and amplitude after the same recording and observation filters.
tests.limits: Instantaneous field asymmetry is not the same as preserved crustal asymmetry. Recording efficiency can mimic field geometry.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Hemispheric dynamo in a full sphere
tests.role: Field geometry and early boundary state
tests.claim: A core without a solid inner core could generate a hemispheric field under asymmetric forcing.
tests.test: Reproduce the dependence on forcing and averaging window, then connect to a dated acquisition kernel.
tests.required_inputs: Full-sphere solutions, forcing amplitudes, polarity histories and rock cooling durations.
tests.discriminator: Compare models using the same averaging statistic, acquisition window and spatial observation operator.
tests.limits: Not every simulated regime reverses. Averaging over a limited interval can strengthen asymmetry; averaging many reversals can weaken the field. Present structure does not fix early structure.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Impact-driven hemispheric forcing
tests.claim: An impact could generate asymmetric core–mantle heat flow.
tests.test: Model the lifetime and transport of the thermal anomaly before coupling it to field generation and recording.
tests.required_inputs: Impact geometry, mantle mixing, boundary heat-flow evolution and remanence ages.
tests.discriminator: The anomaly must reach the core boundary with adequate amplitude and duration at the recording time.
tests.limits: A present mantle asymmetry is not a dated measurement of the ancient core-boundary condition.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Axial mean field with an independent reversal history
tests.claim: A mean field aligned with the rotation axis may have stable or changing polarity.
tests.test: Infer palaeodirections with source-geometry and local-rotation uncertainty; fit polarity changes separately.
tests.required_inputs: Oriented magnetic directions, ages, crustal rotations and source assumptions.
tests.discriminator: A single axial geometry must be compared with alternatives after propagating the same directional uncertainties.
tests.limits: Axial does not mean non-reversing. A reversal changes polarity and does not by itself refute axial symmetry.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Lineations from reversals and crustal growth
tests.claim: Spatial magnetic bands may record polarity changes as crust forms.
tests.test: Test predicted spacing, paired structure and timing against lithology and independent tectonic evidence.
tests.required_inputs: Resolved vector fields, crustal ages, geological boundaries and acquisition models.
tests.discriminator: A proposed growth history must predict the observed pattern beyond the bands used to fit it.
tests.limits: Reversals do not prove seafloor spreading, and lineations can have non-tectonic sources.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Multipolar or non-axial field
tests.claim: Non-dipolar fields may explain directional or spatial complexity.
tests.test: Compare field geometries with identical source and uncertainty models using observations held out from fitting.
tests.required_inputs: Directional data, source depths, recording times and local rotations.
tests.discriminator: Additional field complexity should improve independent predictions, not merely fit uncertain source parameters.
tests.limits: Different ages, local rotations and poorly constrained source geometry can mimic non-axial behavior.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.

tests.title: Hydrothermal creation of remanence
tests.claim: Fluid-driven mineral growth could create or modify a magnetic record.
tests.test: Date magnetic mineral growth and test whether the inferred fluid chemistry and available field permit acquisition.
tests.required_inputs: Carrier mineralogy, reaction path, alteration age and field origin.
tests.discriminator: A proposed chemical remanence requires the appropriate carrier to grow during the candidate field interval.
tests.limits: Surface evidence for water does not specify deep carrier abundance; primary/secondary remanence does not uniquely identify the field source.
tests.building_block: Existing alteration maps provide spatial context only; no fluid-reaction or chemical-remanence model has been run.

tests.title: Hydrothermal destruction of remanence
tests.claim: Alteration could remove or transform magnetic carriers and weaken the record.
tests.test: Compare alteration and magnetic contrasts while controlling geology, depth and resolution; model carrier-specific reactions.
tests.required_inputs: Fluid chemistry, mineral transformations, timing and matched spatial sampling.
tests.discriminator: Destruction must affect enough source volume at the right time to explain the contrast without contradicting mineralogical observations.
tests.limits: Fluids may create as well as destroy carriers. Spatial association alone is not a causal test.
tests.building_block: The regional study measures contrasts and sensitivity to reference terrain; it does not demonstrate hydrothermal erasure.

tests.title: Shock remanence and shock resetting
tests.claim: An impact may acquire, erase or modify remanence through pressure and associated heating.
tests.test: Use carrier-specific pressure/coercivity constraints with an impact pressure–temperature history and an explicit ambient field.
tests.required_inputs: Shock path, grain properties, field origin, relaxation and post-shock preservation.
tests.discriminator: The modeled shock response must reproduce component survival and acquisition for the same minerals and pressures.
tests.limits: A thermal pulse is not a shock-remanence model. Laboratory effects require mineral-specific scaling.
tests.building_block: The existing reheating scenario is a synthetic conductive thermal experiment; it includes no pressure or shock physics.

tests.title: Burial, mineralogy and observation height
tests.claim: A common dynamo could leave different measured fields because the magnetic archives and viewing geometry differ.
tests.test: Compare shared-field and different-field histories using the same source geometry, acquisition and instrument response; perform signal-injection recovery tests.
tests.required_inputs: Source volume, mineral abundance, burial, observation altitude, noise and recording history.
tests.discriminator: A shared-field model must predict independent regional contrasts with physically admissible source properties.
tests.limits: Equivalent magnetic depths are not directly layer thicknesses or Curie depths. A local surface measurement is not a global hemispheric mean.
tests.building_block: Regional altitude/reference sensitivity and the synthetic thermal gate are available separately. No joint magnetic inversion has been run.

tests.title: Present-day degree-one mantle structure
tests.claim: A present thermal asymmetry may constrain interior evolution models relevant to the dichotomy.
tests.test: Compare evolution histories that reach the inferred present structure and test their ancient magnetic predictions separately.
tests.required_inputs: Tidal inversion uncertainties, material properties, mantle evolution and independently dated remanence.
tests.discriminator: A history should fit both present interior constraints and ancient observations without treating them as simultaneous measurements.
tests.limits: Present mantle structure does not directly demonstrate ancient core heat flow, a particular dynamo geometry or crustal demagnetization.
tests.building_block: No corresponding physical model has been run in this project.
